title: Zeros at the End of 100!
statement: How many zeros does $100!$ end with?
insight: Each trailing zero needs a factor 10 = 2·5, and fives are scarcer. Count multiples of 5, then extra fives from multiples of 25.
hints: A trailing zero is a factor of 10. Which prime is the bottleneck?
Numbers like 25 and 75 contribute two fives.
solution: Trailing zeros = number of factors of 5 in $100!$ (twos are plentiful): $\lfloor 100/5\rfloor + \lfloor 100/25\rfloor = 20 + 4 = 24$.
